sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  1/9  CMA  For Appellants : Mr. Amar Dineshbhai Pandiya.

For Respondents : Mr. M. Jayaraj for R2.
 R1 - Exparte.

R. Gowthami vs V. Viswanathan on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194025655/
1  JUDGMENT

The appeal has been filed by the appellants challenging the award passed by the Tribunal in M.C.O.P. No. 9161 of 2015 dated 07.10.2021.
2.The

appellants had filed a claim petition before the Tribunal stating that on 09.11.2015, while the deceased was riding the motor cycle bearing Registration No. TN 05 K 4557 on Venkodu Salai near water pumping house, a HGV Tanker lorry bearing Registration No. TN 39 AS 2147 belonging to the first respondent driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motor cycle, as a result of which the deceased sustained severe injuries and died on the spot.
Thus, the appellants filed claim petition claiming compensation.
3.The second respondent filed counter denying all the averments made in the claim petition.

It is stated that the accident occurred only https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis due to the rash and negligent riding of the deceased and the claim petition is bad for non-joinder of the owner and insurer of the motor cycle.
Further, it is stated that the deceased was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
In any case, the compensation claimed was excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
4.The first respondent remained exparte before the Tribunal.
5.The appellants examined two witnesses as PW1 and PW2 on their side and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.24.
Neither witness has been examined nor document has been marked on the side of the respondents.

6.The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the lorry belonging to the first respondent and fixed 90% contributory negligence on the driver of the lorry and 10% contributory negligence on the deceased for not wearing helmet at the time of accident and directed the second respondent to pay a sum of Rs.24,16,100/- as compensation to the appellants.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellants have preferred the instant appeal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

7.The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the Tribunal had fixed a very meagre notional income at Rs.12,051/- by only considering the cost inflation index and ignoring the evidence adduced on the side of the appellants.
The deceased was survived by his wife and two children.
His wife was pregnant at the time of his death and the third child was born after his death.
Hence, the Tribunal ought to have fixed higher notional income.

As regards the compensation under the head Loss of love and affection, the Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.40,000/- each totaling a sum of Rs.2,40,000/- to the appellants, since at the time of his death, the father of the deceased was alive.

The learned counsel also submitted that the contributory negligence fixed by the Tribunal @
10% is erroneous and prayed for allowing the appeal.
8.The first respondent remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.

The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that notice to the first respondent may be dispensed with and made an R. Gowthami vs V. Viswanathan on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194025655/
2 endorsement to that effect in the court bundle.
Hence, notice to the first respondent is dispensed with.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

9.The learned counsel for the second respondent submitted that thought the appellants claimed that the deceased was working as head cook, there is no proof either to establish the avocation or the income of the deceased.
In the absence of the same, the Tribunal was right in fixing the notional income at Rs.12,051/-.
The deceased did not wear helmet at the time of accident.
Hence, the Tribunal had rightly fixed 10% contributory negligence on the deceased.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

10.The questions involved in the instant appeal are;
(i) Whether the Tribunal is right in fixing the contributory negligence @ 10% on the deceased?
(ii) Whether the compensation awarded is just and reasonable?
11.(i)On perusal of Ex.P.5, Postmortem certificate, it is seen that the deceased died due to head injuries.
Had he worn helmet at the time of accident, he could have avoided head injuries.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the deceased and the evidence adduced on the side of the appellants, the Tribunal was right in fixing 10% towards contributory negligence on the deceased.
Hence, 10% has to be deducted https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis towards contributory negligence on the award amount.
11.(ii) This Court finds that the appellants had examined the wife of the deceased as PW1 to show that the deceased was working as head cook.
However, no proof has been filed to establish the income though it is claimed that he has earned Rs.15,000/- per month.
Considering the age of the deceased, year of the accident and the avocation, this Court is the view that it would be reasonable to fix Rs.13,000/- as notional monthly income.
Since the deceased was aged 27 years at the time of the accident, the appellants are entitled to 40% enhancement towards future prospects and the multiplier applicable is 17.
There are five dependents and hence 1/5th has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Hence, the loss of income would be Rs.13,000/- + Rs.5,200 (40% of Rs.13,000)
= Rs.18,200/- X 12 X 17 X 4/5 = Rs.29,70,240/-.

The appellants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the other head loss of love and affection and thus, the appellants are entitled to Rs.2,00,000/-
under the said head.
The award under the other heads are just and the same are confirmed.

Thus,
the award of the Tribunal is modified as follows;

 1. Loss of income 25,81,324 29,70,240   2. Loss of love and affection 40,000 2,00,000
3 . Loss of estate 15,000 15,000
4. Medical Bills 33,212 33,212
5. Funeral expenses 15,000 15,000
Total 26,84,536 32,33,452 E  R  10% Contributory 2,68,453 3,23,345  Negligence
Net Compensation 24,16,082 29,10,106  rounded off rounded off   to 24,16,100 to 29,10,100 12.

With the above modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.24,16,100/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.29,10,100/-
together with interest at 7.5% per annum (excluding the default period, if any) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The second respondent is directed to deposit the award amount now determined by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any,

On such deposit, the appellants 1 and 4 are permitted to withdraw their respective shares on the basis of apportionment fixed by the Tribunal along with proportionate interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.

The shares of the minor appellants 2, 3 and 5 are directed to be deposited in the interest bearing Fixed Deposit in any of the nationalized bank till they attain the age of majority and the first appellant is permitted to withdraw the accrued interest once in three months.
The appellants are directed to pay necessary Court fee, if any on the enhanced compensation.
No costs.
